conventions.convention: Local finiteness requires finite positive homotopy groups and eventual vanishing at each basepoint; no uniform truncation bound or finite component set is required. Homotopy weights are the products of |π_i| with exponent (−1)^i. Proper means that every homotopy fiber has finitely many components.

The base is a finite field; differentials have cohomological degree +1. Right-module differentiation uses d(mf)=d(m)f+(−1)^|m|m d(f). Local finiteness means finite total Hom cohomology for each pair, without a uniform degree bound. The supplied enhancement includes stable module and diagram homotopy theories and functorial homotopy cofibers.

The first derived Hall input is the source and the second is the homotopy cofiber: χ_x*χ_y counts arrows x→z with cofiber isomorphic to y. Source and cofiber are restricted to isomorphism classes, without chosen framings. Coefficients lie in Q.

The ordinary supplier counts the second input as subobject and the first as quotient, so the heart basis map is an anti-homomorphism, equivalently an embedding of the opposite Hall algebra. The theorem assumes a bounded t-structure, a small finitary hereditary heart, and the stated exact realization equivalence.

load_bearing.statement: A locally finite small dg-category over a finite field has finite-dimensional total Hom cohomology for every pair. The supplied enhancement includes stable projective module homotopy theory, the corresponding diagram homotopy theories, functorial homotopy cofibers, and the stated mapping-space and core homotopy-group identifications.

For any two perfect right dg modules x,y over a locally finite dg-category over F_q, the graded vector space ⊕_i Ext^i(x,y) is finite-dimensional. In particular, every Ext group is finite and all but finitely many vanish.

For a locally finite dg-enhancement, X^(0), X^(1), and X^(2) are locally finite; s×t is proper on components; consequently the defining pull-push expression is a well-defined product on finite-support functions.

For a map f:X→Y of locally finite homotopy types, the total weight of fiber components over y mapping to x equals w_X(x)/w_Y(y). Thus f_!(α)(y)=Σ_{f(x)=y}α(x)w_X(x)/w_Y(y); every homotopy fiber is locally finite and the defining weighted sum is finite.
The arrow-composition square and the composite-cofiber square displayed in the item are homotopy cartesian.
The homotopy weight of the target-fiber component represented by f:x→z is |Aut(f/z)|^−1 times ∏_{i>0}|Ext^−i(x,z)|^((−1)^i)|Ext^−i(x,x)|^((−1)^(i+1)).

For perfect modules x,y,z, g^z_{x,y}=|[x,z]_y|∏_{i>0}|Ext^−i(x,z)|^((−1)^i) divided by |Aut(x)|∏_{i>0}|Ext^−i(x,x)|^((−1)^i), equivalently the stated sum of stabilizer reciprocals times the same higher-Ext correction.

Under the stated locally finite enhancement, bounded t-structure, finitary hereditary heart and exact realization hypotheses, [M]↦χ_M is an injective algebra anti-homomorphism from the untwisted Hall algebra, equivalently an embedding of its opposite; its image is the span of heart classes.

published_dependencies.used_for: Mapping-path model for homotopy fibers. The owned definition explicitly extends the based supplier to unbased fibers and empty-source cases.
Replacing a map by a homotopy-equivalent total space followed by a Hurewicz fibration.
Fiber-group finiteness, alternating order cancellation, and the component action and stabilizer needed for fiber weights.

Using the finite field as the commutative base ring for dg algebras and modules.
Vocabulary for the projective module model structure explicitly supplied by the enhancement.
Triangulated structure, translation and distinguished-triangle conventions.
Heart and orthogonality conventions used to eliminate negative Ext between heart objects.
Shifted truncation subcategories and bounded t-structure conventions.
Projectivity and the two lifting steps in the A2 resolution calculation.

seams_checked.note: The supplier definitions and finiteness/associativity results were opened. The heart theorem preserves their quotient-first, subobject-second convention by stating an opposite-algebra embedding.

The DGA and dg-module definitions were opened. The enhancement preserves the degree +1 differential, composition Leibniz sign, and separate right-module sign; it explicitly supplies the additional stable homotopy-theory structure.

The page and rem-derived-and-cohomological-hall-are-distinct were opened. They describe perfect-module cores and higher homotopy weights faithfully and do not use derived Hall theory to supply motivic convolution or integration.

The page and rem-finite-quiver-hall-counts-and-dt-bps-interpretation were opened. Derived Hall theory is identified as separate reading context with dg enhancements and higher homotopy weights; its theorems are not claimed as premises for the finite-field wall-crossing proof.
